architecturePolicies.limit: Project policy, broader than the upstream factory-only rules. Configure paths for managed components, not adapters or pure value modules. Erased TypeScript typeof type queries are admitted; executable typeof expressions and value references beside type annotations remain checked.

Identifies the first inline arrow/function creator argument through literal dot/bracket/template members, optional calls, comments and parenthesized/as/satisfies/non-null wrappers. Also follows an immutable const initialized with an arrow/function expression when its direct first-argument reference follows initialization in the same lexical scope. A direct call of that name in the same scope, a declaration export or a local named/default value export removes the root exception. Type-only exports and foreign re-exports do not export the local creator; nested calls, other escapes and full call-graph ownership remain unresolved. Extra callbacks and leading spreads do not establish ownership. Strict policy over selected paths, including local classes; scope out value-only modules deliberately. Exclusive ownership of declared/exported creators, aliases, mutable/cross-scope/imported creators, dynamic/escaped names, generators, type assertions, indirect values and returned-constructor value wrappers remain unresolved.

Value named imports, including renamed imports, and direct namespace dot/bracket references and object destructuring are checked. Type-only imports, unrelated namespaces and lexical shadowing are admitted. Namespace aliases, computed members, dynamic/CommonJS imports and re-export barrels still need data-flow/import-graph coverage; nested-block var hoisting remains conservative.
This is an explicit project import-graph policy. It requires a declared core layer and allowed edges; it does not infer the library receiver type.
Closed package export paths are verified for the pinned 0.1.3-beta package. New package versions require renewed source review.

deliveryRequirements.limit: These project evidence requirements preserve published delivery and exception behavior. Source canaries establish the upstream contrast, not compliance of a consuming project. Applicability and failing controls must be reviewed with the project's actual call paths, lifetime and configured adapters.

requirements.verify: Assert actual argument delivery and result use, including default-parameter arity. If an asynchronous dependency is intentional, declare its promise contract and await it at the consuming boundary with an owned failure policy. The pinned runtime invokes creators according to Function.length and returns their result without awaiting it. Verify effects through the injected ports.
canaries: two-argument factory
first default suppresses injection
async creator resolution returns its promise without awaiting it
generator creator resolution returns an unstarted iterator

requirements.statement: Required creation verification must complete before a value is admitted to use. A verification callback must reject a failed invariant by throwing; a false return is not rejection. A configured system factory must satisfy the actual contract used by its consumers, not only callable-member admission.
requirements.when: Creation has an output invariant or the product replaces a system dependency.
requirements.verify: Assert rejection, completion order and required output behavior through actual resolution. An async verification callback is not awaited; a generator body does not run. The pinned runtime ignores verification return values and checks only selected callable members on system outputs. Failed singleton verification is not cached; test subsequent attempts and effect repeat safety.
canaries: synchronous verification finishes before resolution returns
async verification finishes after the created value escapes
false verification return does not reject creation
failed singleton verification is retried instead of cached
custom queue callable admission does not verify public size flush or result contracts
custom event bus promise preserves blocking completion
custom event bus void breaks blocking completion
custom message bus promise preserves blocking completion
custom message bus void breaks blocking completion
event subscription registry owns snapshots aggregation and removal
message subscription registry owns snapshots aggregation and removal

requirements.statement: A dependency owner must choose transient or singleton lifetime and must verify the resulting identity, shared mutation and scope. A singleton must not hold one user's or organization's mutable state for unrelated callers. Resolution failure must have an owned retry and effect policy.
requirements.when: A dependency is resolved repeatedly, shared across requests or materialized as a singleton.
requirements.verify: Assert repeated transient creation, singleton identity, actual constructor input and ownership of mutable fields. Exercise failed creation and null or undefined singleton results. The pinned singleton rejects only nullish results and caches other values; a transient can return null. A successful registration is not successful materialization.
canaries: transients recreate while singletons retain identity
singleton null rejection does not remove its registration
singleton false is cached while transient null is returned

requirements.statement: Force replacement must be confined to an owned test runtime. A replacement must not be treated as disposal or revocation of previously returned instances. The bootstrap-owned kernel must not be replaced through public admission.
requirements.when: Tests use force registration or retain dependencies across replacement.
requirements.verify: Assert production-mode rejection, test-mode replacement and ownership of the retired instance. The pinned force singleton operation removes its cache entry but does not dispose the old value; retained references remain live. Follow the supported injected kernel instead of relying on a warning to reject reserved admission.
canaries: singleton force registration in run
singleton force replacement leaves the old instance live and undisposed
bootstrap kernel public registerSingleton

requirements.statement: The application must own shutdown and test-reset boundaries. Shutdown must stop new application work and settle or cancel owned work and resources according to a named budget. Runtime shutdown or test reset alone must not be treated as disposal, drained handlers or revoked retained references.
requirements.when: The product stops, resets a test runtime or replaces a runtime while references or work can remain live.
requirements.verify: Exercise the actual application's admission barrier, retained references, resource disposal, pending work and failure deadline. The pinned shutdown only records a flag; old runtime references still resolve after shutdown or global reset. Reset creates a new global runtime but does not revoke previous application references. Verify inspector closure separately.
canaries: runtime shutdown still permits resolution without disposal
test reset creates a new runtime while retained references stay live

requirements.statement: A domain boundary must validate the complete admitted value and its bounds. TypeCompatibilityCheck and DCast must not be treated as strict type, complete collection or domain validation.
requirements.when: The product uses compatibility or conversion helpers to admit external or stored values.
requirements.verify: Test actual strict types, every collection item, numeric precision and domain constraints. Own input depth and size budgets; recursive compatibility on a cyclic object can overflow the stack. Compatibility admits numeric strings, inspects only the first array element, and can match an object's keys without validating field values. Boolean conversion of the strings false and no returns true. Reject unsafe values before the domain decision.
canaries: compatibility is coercion-compatible while false text converts to true
array compatibility checks the first element instead of the full collection
object compatibility matches keys without admitting field values
bigint conversion to number can lose integer precision
compatibility recursion requires an owned input depth budget

requirements.statement: A conversion caller must choose an explicit target order and verify the actual returned type and domain value. A TypeScript generic argument must not be treated as a runtime output guarantee.
requirements.when: The product consumes a DCast result or supplies more than one conversion target.
requirements.verify: Exercise the selected targets in their real order and assert the result before use. Verify the configured DCast replacement as well as the default. The first successful target wins; a generic can claim string while the selected number target returns a number. Include reversed-order and wrong-result-type controls.
canaries: conversion target order chooses the first successful representation
declared generic does not control the runtime cast target
bigint target does not use general numeric coercion

requirements.statement: A conversion boundary must have an explicit policy for absent values, fallback values and exceptions. A fallback must satisfy the consumer's domain contract. A fallback must not be assumed to handle every conversion failure.
requirements.when: DCast can receive nullish or invalid data or a caller supplies a fallback.
requirements.verify: Test null, undefined, unsupported conversion, absent and explicit fallback, malformed target configuration and native conversion exceptions. The pinned runtime returns nullish input even for a different requested target, returns a supplied fallback without converting or copying it, and validates target shape before fallback. An invalid Date can throw despite a fallback.
canaries: nullish cast input is returned even for a number target
fallback is returned without conversion or ownership isolation
invalid target configuration rejects before applying fallback
undefined fallback does not suppress an unsupported conversion
invalid Date can escape a date target or throw before string fallback

requirements.statement: A date boundary must name the admitted date format, calendar validity, time basis and mutation owner. A returned Date must be verified before use and must not be assumed to be a fresh immutable value.
requirements.when: The product uses date or formatted-date DCast targets.
requirements.verify: Exercise explicit ymd, dmy and mdy metadata on ambiguous input and reject invalid calendar dates. Assert the UTC representation where this contract requires it. The pinned runtime passes a Date through by identity, including an invalid Date for the date target; formatted output can fail. Copy or own mutable dates when they cross a sharing boundary.
canaries: explicit date metadata gives distinct UTC interpretations of ambiguous input
explicit date parsing rejects an invalid calendar date
explicit ymd metadata preserves a valid leap day and rejects an invalid one
unknown date metadata silently uses mdy interpretation
date conversion retains the mutable input Date by identity
invalid Date can escape a date target or throw before string fallback

requirements.statement: An array passed to DCast must be an intentional value-and-format tuple. A caller must not use this argument as a whole-collection conversion. Tuple contents and metadata must be validated before use.
requirements.when: The product passes array or tuple input to DCast.
requirements.verify: Assert the actual value at index zero and format metadata at index one. Verify collections item by item through an owned bounded operation instead. The pinned runtime takes the first array item as the value, treats the second as metadata and ignores later items; an empty array becomes undefined.
canaries: cast array input converts only its first item
empty array cast input becomes undefined
unknown date metadata silently uses mdy interpretation

requirements.statement: A field-helper caller must distinguish absence, null and valid falsy values and must validate the actual output. Inherited fields, shared references and callback failures must have an explicit admission and ownership policy.
requirements.when: The product uses withDefaultValue or straightValue on domain or configuration data.
requirements.verify: Test missing, null, undefined, zero, false and empty text. The pinned withDefaultValue keeps nonnull falsy values but straightValue returns undefined for them. Both accept inherited fields; withDefaultValue does not perform its documented expected-type check and its callback exceptions propagate. Verify returned references and defaults independently of generic types.
canaries: field helpers distinguish nullish defaults from valid falsy values differently
field helpers admit inherited fields and retain object references
field default helper does not check expected types and applies only its callback
field callback failures propagate instead of returning the default
straight field access rejects missing dictionaries or fields

requirements.statement: A product that needs a priority queue must select and verify an actual implementation. The IPriorityQueue declaration and QueuePriorities values must not be treated as an available queue instance or a tested scheduling policy.
requirements.when: The product promises priority ordering or consumes an IPriorityQueue implementation.
requirements.verify: Verify the selected adapter's ordering between and within priorities, capacity, starvation decision, peek and stream views, clearing and per-priority flush. Assert named DPriority inputs and any numeric-rank translation. The pinned package exports numeric ranks and a type-only interface, with no public priority-queue constructor; its built-in IQueue remains FIFO. Own configuration instead of trusting readonly types to freeze runtime values.
canaries: priority ranks are numeric and runtime values are mutable
published runtime has no priority-queue constructor or interface value
built-in queue preserves FIFO regardless of payload priority

requirements.statement: A priority-queue producer must validate the named priority before admission, await enqueue and handle a false result with an explicit reject, retry or backpressure policy. Numeric QueuePriorities ranks must not be forwarded as DPriority names. IQueue must not be called with the IPriorityQueue argument order.
requirements.when: The product submits work through an IPriorityQueue adapter or translates external priority data into queue calls.
requirements.verify: Hold actual admission and verify that the producer does not report acceptance early. Reject invalid or numeric priorities before adapter use, handle false and propagate the owned failure policy. The priority interface expects name then item; the built-in IQueue expects only the item and stores a supplied priority string as work. Include missing-await, ignored-false, invalid-name and wrong-adapter controls.
canaries: priority ranks are numeric and runtime values are mutable
built-in queue stores the priority argument when called as a priority adapter

requirements.statement: Interaction declarations and graph metadata must match the owned application contract. A declaration or diagram must not be treated as proof that an effect occurred or that an architecture rule was satisfied.
requirements.when: The product declares interactions or uses dependency information or a graph as architecture evidence.
requirements.verify: Compare declared and actual registered interactions with a bounded application test. Keep declared, observed and omitted behavior distinct. Test the actual metadata ownership policy: snapshots copy top-level collections but can retain nested metadata references. Validate and redact labels and metadata before sharing them.
canaries: graph declarations do not prove an interaction occurred
declaration snapshots isolate top level but retain nested metadata

requirements.statement: A graph query must have an explicit input, cost and result-scope policy. Query filters and degrees of separation must not be used as tenant isolation or authorization.
requirements.when: The product accepts graph queries, seed identifiers, diagram filters or regular-expression operators.
requirements.verify: Test admitted fields, empty groups, unknown seeds, include/exclude precedence, views and the actual undirected expansion through connector nodes. Bound query size, degree, pattern cost and response size outside the pinned implementation. An empty include group matches every node. Reject unauthorized requests before graph construction; filtering alone cannot grant access.
canaries: an empty graph query group matches every graph node
a graph request with an unknown seed returns no nodes

requirements.statement: A graph consumer must verify the returned graph and own timeout and readiness failures. A matching request identifier must not be treated as authenticated response provenance.
requirements.when: The product calls requestGraph or supplies observability buses, handlers or engine lifecycle controls.
requirements.verify: Verify actual wiring and a valid response contract. Test missing, paused and unwired responders, malformed results and forged matching identifiers. The pinned monitor uses predictable request counters, accepts a matching payload without graph validation and rejects after five seconds when no response arrives. Own any shorter operation budget and cancellation policy; a caller timeout alone does not cancel the underlying request.
canaries: graph correlation accepts a matching response without validating the graph
an unwired graph engine reaches its owned request timeout

requirements.statement: Monitor and inspector diagnostics must not be the sole source of a complete, immutable security audit. A subscriber must own its completion, failures and unsubscribe operation.
requirements.when: The product consumes onActionOccurred, observed graph activity or inspection recordings for operational or audit decisions.
requirements.verify: Test the required application events independently of diagnostic filters, pause controls and first-seen graph aggregation. The pinned monitor omits system identifiers and emits asynchronously; observed graph maps keep the first occurrence. Recording arrays and payload references are mutable. Use an owned durable audit channel when the product needs complete, tamper-resistant evidence.
canaries: inspection exposes a mutable recording array
inspector retains two events and removes its monitor observer

requirements.statement: The inspector must remain an explicitly admitted development diagnostic. Access to its recording, commands and graph endpoints must be protected independently of CORS and the production environment flag.
requirements.when: The product starts or exposes the dcouplr inspector.
requirements.verify: Verify the actual environment, host binding, reachable network and access owner before startup. Reject production use even if NODE_ENV is absent or incorrect. Loopback is the default, but another host can be configured. The pinned startup rejects exact NODE_ENV=production; a denied preflight does not prevent direct POST commands or recording GET. Validate commands and results rather than treating every ok response as an applied command.
canaries: inspector origin policy is not authorization
inspector refuses a production runtime before opening a server
unknown inspector commands report success without changing capture

requirements.statement: Inspection data must have an explicit redaction, serialization, ownership and retention policy before capture or export. An event-count limit must not be treated as a byte budget.
requirements.when: The product captures, exports or shares diagnostic events.
requirements.verify: Test actual confidential fields and large or cyclic payloads before they reach the inspector. The pinned normalizer retains raw payload and detail references without redaction. Recording retains a bounded count only for a valid finite budget; one event can contain unbounded bytes and cyclic data can fail JSON serialization. Do not use mutable captured references as an admitted export value.
canaries: inspection normalization retains secrets and shared references
inspection event count does not bound the bytes of one event
a cyclic inspection payload makes recording serialization fail
infinite inspector budget disables bounded retention

requirements.statement: An inspector owner must await close and verify cleanup on successful startup, failed startup and shutdown. A failed bind must not be assumed to remove an observer created before listening.
requirements.when: The product owns an inspector server or retries its startup.
requirements.verify: Exercise occupied-port failure, repeated startup and actual shutdown. The pinned implementation subscribes before listening and does not undo that subscription on bind failure. Await the returned close promise after successful startup. Prevent uncontrolled retries or supply reviewed ownership for leaked observers; runtime reset alone is not evidence that asynchronous close completed.
canaries: inspector bind failure leaves its already-created observer subscribed
inspector retains two events and removes its monitor observer

requirements.statement: A diagnostic transport or diagram consumer must own request, stream and rendering budgets and safe rendering of untrusted labels. Mermaid text must not be treated as sanitized HTML.
requirements.when: The product exposes inspection HTTP or SSE routes or renders interactionGraphToMermaid output.
requirements.verify: Bound HTTP body bytes and time, connected clients, replay bytes and slow-client buffers at an admitted boundary. The pinned inspector accumulates command bodies and writes SSE without an owned client/backpressure budget. The graph renderer escapes quotes and backslashes and handles reserved node IDs, but preserves markup in labels. Verify the selected rendering engine and its security configuration; source text alone cannot certify browser safety.
canaries: Mermaid text is not an HTML sanitizer
inspection event count does not bound the bytes of one event
